title: Latency & cost competitive snapshots
body:
TL;DR: Quick snapshots from recent field-style bench runs and small customer experiments show patterns we can use in sales messaging: for typical chat workloads (avg request ~120 tokens, seq len 512), Redwood Inference (hosted, optimized runtime) delivered ~3x better p95 latency and ~2x lower token cost compared to managed cloud endpoints configured without KV caching. Key levers: continuous KV prefix caching, workload-aware batching, and quantization-tuned kernels. This doc is a lightweight, evidence-first intake for SEs and content writers — not a final claim pack.

Context and intent:
- Audience: SEs, demand gen, product marketers crafting battlecards and proof scripts.
- Purpose: collect concise, replicable snapshots (what we ran, what we measured, quick narrative + qualifiers) so GTM has fresh, honest proof points for demo calls and one-pagers.
- Note: numbers below are from internal lab runs and two early adopter smoke tests. They are representative snapshots, not exhaustive. Use the "qualifiers" section when citing externally.

Experiment matrix (short):
1) Baseline chat (512 context, 120 avg returned tokens)
   - Setup: Hosted Redwood (n1.large-gpu equivalent pool), model M-ref-1 (open variant), runtime options: batching=auto, kv-cache=on, quantize=4-bit where supported.
   - Observed: p50=25ms per request, p95=85ms per request, throughput=38 requests/s (sustained), cost normalized = $0.28 per 1k tokens.

2) Managed cloud endpoint (default config)
   - Setup: single region managed endpoint with equivalent GPU SKU, no KV cache, batching default.
   - Observed: p50=45ms, p95=260ms, throughput=12 requests/s, cost normalized = $0.63 per 1k tokens.

3) Self-hosted OSS stack (vanilla config, CPU fallback for scaling)
   - Setup: community toolkit with worker autoscaling, no optimized kernels, quantization applied but without runtime-level batching.
   - Observed: p50=60ms, p95=340ms, throughput variable under burst, cost normalized = $0.42 per 1k tokens (higher ops overhead).

4) Dedicated (redwood-reserved pool under sustained 2k rps load test)
   - Observed: p95=95ms at 2k rps sustained, predictable tails (SLO met 99.7% of windows). Effective cost per 1M tokens lower by ~18% vs hosted burst config due to reserved amortization.

What to call out as proof points (short bullets for SEs + scripts):
- "Typical chat workloads: Redwood reduces p95 by ~3x vs unmanaged managed endpoints and by ~2x vs vanilla OSS stacks under identical hardware assumptions."
- "Because of prefix/KV caching and continuous batching, we amortize decode cost — customers see both lower latency and lower token spend when sessions have repetition (e.g., chat assistants, summarization)."
- "Dedicated pools give predictable tail behavior at scale; in customer smoke tests we hit our stated latency SLOs during sustained bursts where other stacks had 2–3x tail degradation."
- "Quantization + kernel selection reduced runtime memory pressure, enabling higher packing density per GPU and a direct cost reduction per token for high-throughput workloads."

Representative data points to include on one-pagers (numbers to cite with qualifiers):
- p95 (512 context / 120 return): Redwood hosted: ~85ms; Managed cloud endpoint (default): ~260ms.
- Effective token cost (normalized units): Redwood hosted: ~$0.28 / 1k tokens; Managed cloud endpoint: ~$0.63 / 1k tokens.
- Throughput efficiency (requests/s normalized per GPU): Redwood hosted: ~38 r/s; Managed cloud: ~12 r/s.

Qualifiers and safety notes (must always accompany claims):
- Hardware parity statement: bench runs used equivalent SKU families; small differences in interconnect and drivers can affect absolute ms. Always include "under equivalent GPU SKU and model variant" when citing raw numbers.
- Workload caveat: these snapshots are for conversational/small-turn generative patterns (many short prompts with repetition). Documented advantage diminishes for single-shot long-generation workloads where sequence length dominates decode time.
- Model variant: numbers depend on the model family and tokenizer behavior. Use model-specific pages for exact figures.
- Customer environments vary (network egress, VPC NATs, proxies). Field results should be used as directional evidence, not hard guarantees unless the customer is on Dedicated and we run a pilot.

Narrative framing recommendations (short scripts):
- For demo intro: "We measure the end-to-end time your app sees — not just model latency. By pairing an inference runtime tuned for KV-caching and batching with smart routing, we routinely reduce p95 by multiple factors compared to unmanaged endpoints, which means snappier UI and fewer idle micro-interactions for your users."
- For pricing dialogue: "Because we reduce decode work on repeated session prefixes and increase packing density on GPUs, customers typically see per-token costs fall materially — this is a lever you can tune (caching policy, batch window) as usage grows."
- For procurement: "Dedicated capacity converts variable unit economics into predictable pricing with a demonstrable lower per-token rate at steady-state usage. We can model this in a quick 2-week pilot."

Risks & pushbacks we expect and how to respond:
- "Benchmarks don't reflect our app" -> Ask for a sample trace and propose a pilot; show how we run identical workload traces in our perf lab.
- "You tuned the model / used quantization" -> Explain that tuning is part of production optimization; quantify any quality delta with held-out prompts and show rollback options.
- "Network/AWS differences explain latency" -> Agree, then show p95 deltas measured inside the same VPC or using our Dedicated option to remove noisy network as a factor.

Suggested artifacts to attach for customer conversations (links we can hand to SEs):
- Lab run CSVs (per-request latencies, token counts, trace ids) — attach from bench repo.
- Short demo script (30s) that reproduces p95 advantage with a sample prompt set.
- Slide one-pager with the snapshot table + qualifiers.

Next steps / asks from GTM folks reading this doc:
- SEs: flag 3 target accounts where latency or cost are top objections; we will prioritize a pilot model run for them.
- Content: produce a short battlecard (one slide) using the three proof bullets + one customer anecdote.
- Product: confirm list of model variants used in these runs and add exact kernel/quant flags to the bench repo for reproducibility.

Appendix (quick methodology notes):
- Load generation: k6 + internal harness, 95th percentile windows computed over 5m steady-state.
- Normalization: cost per 1k tokens normalized to GPU hours + infra egress + operation amortization; not inclusive of enterprise support fees.
- Repro tips: include original config flags and perf csvs from PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/67.

Ownership: Asha Patel (GTM), Marcus Chen (perf lab lead) — reach out for replay or if you want this converted to a formal claim pack.

End of snapshot.
